name: sol_am_replayattack_1
description: Missing replay protection allows signed/failed transactions to be re-executed
question: The source file in `source` implements a function that executes an action based on a signed message, meta-transaction, or transaction record (e.g., executeTransaction, permit, relay) and fails to permanently invalidate that message or transaction after it is processed or attempted, such as by never checking/incrementing a nonce or never marking a transaction hash as used, so the same signed payload or transaction can be resubmitted and replayed to re-trigger the action, excluding cases where a nonce or used-flag is correctly incremented/set before any external call or where the action's own state changes inherently make repetition impossible.
criteria: executeTransaction verifies a signature against signer/threshold but never records or checks a used-transaction hash, allowing the same signed transaction to be replayed after it fails or succeeds
A meta-transaction relay function reads a nonce for signature verification but does not increment or store it anywhere, so the identical signed message can be submitted multiple times
A permit-style function validates an off-chain signature but never marks that signature/nonce as consumed, letting it be reused indefinitely
Nonce is incremented only after an external call that can revert and roll back the increment, letting a failed transaction be resubmitted with the same nonce and signature
